detail.body:
## Motivation

`--dcp-size > 1` does not work for the RoPE DSA models (GLM-5.2, GLM-5.3, DeepSeek-V3.2): the sparse backend returns no LSE, the index-K cache and the MTP draft pool are sized per rank while the allocator hands out widened slots, and the TRT-LLM buffers are sized for one rank's heads. Builds on the approach of #42536 (co-authored with @vincentzed) and the Flash stack #40433 / #40434.

## Modifications

- **Target KV** stays striped by position (unchanged `main` layout). The **index-K cache is replicated** and addressed by the widened allocator slot, so every rank scores the whole sequence and selects the global top-k.
- **Attention**: one Triton kernel keeps the top-k slots this rank owns, maps them to local rows and compacts them; the TRT-LLM sparse kernel runs on the DCP group's gathered query heads with `return_lse`, and the existing MLA DCP merge combines the partials. Decode, target verify and extend all take this path (no prefix-KV gather). Shared-top-k layers reuse the localized table (21 remaps per step instead of 78).
- **MTP draft (nextn)**: the pool is replicated over the widened slots (`dcp_replicated`, kernel page stays 64) and the draft attends without the DCP group (`is_nextn` / `is_draft_worker`, as the Qwen3.5 draft does), so MTP index share feeds the draft directly.
- **Accounting**: index keys and the draft pool are charged `dcp_size` times per physical token on every platform (the NPU-only guards are dropped).
- **Launch validation**: the generic DCP hook now rejects prefill CP with `--dcp-size > 1`; the DSA override rejects HiSparse, HiCache, PD disaggregation and tree drafting, and defaults the DSA backends to `trtllm` (`index_kpool > 1` was already rejected on `main`).
- **Fast follows** (rejected at launch for now): HiCache and PD disaggregation need the replicated index-K cache's widened page geometry in the host pool and the transfer page-id lists; other DSA backends need to return the LSE under DCP.
- Kept from #42536: the LSE combine keeps all-empty padding rows at zero. Not kept: the head folding for the FlashInfer 0.7.0.post1 `return_lse` bug above 32 heads, which does not reproduce on B300 with that FlashInfer (see the comment below); the gathered heads go to the kernel in one call.

Design notes with permalinks: `dsa-dcp-design.md` (shared separately).

## Accuracy Tests

`zai-org/GLM-5.3` (FP8), 8xB300, `--tp 8 --mem-fraction-static 0.88 --max-running-requests 64`, branch at `28bb3d6074`. MTP = `--speculative-algorithm EAGLE --speculative-num-steps 5 --speculative-eagle-topk 1 --speculative-num-draft-tokens 6`. GSM8K: `few_shot_gsm8k`, 8-shot, 1319 questions. AIME26: `sgl-eval run aime26 --n-repeats 4` with the GLM-5.2-FP8 preset (200k max tokens).

| Config | GSM8K acc | AIME26 pass@1 (avg of 4) | AIME26 pass@4 | AIME26 gen tok/s | MTP accept len |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| TP8 | 0.912 | 99.17% | 100% | 1140 | - |
| TP8 + DCP2 | 0.917 | 99.17% | 100% | 1041 | - |
| TP8 + DCP2 + MTP | 0.919 | 95.83% | 100% | 1876 | 3.51 |
| TP8 + DCP8 | 0.914 | 95.00% | 100% | 838 | - |
| TP8 + DCP8 + MTP | 0.919 | 95.00% | 100% | 1784 | 3.62 |

Spot checks (GSM8K, 300-400 questions): `--dcp-comm-backend ag_rs` DCP2 + MTP 0.907; an 8192-token-per-rank pool so the last allocator page is in use, DCP2 0.903 and DCP2 + MTP 0.907; without head folding, DCP8 0.943 and DCP8 + MTP 0.913 (the 64-head case).

AIME26 pass@1 spread is sampling noise: every run loses problem 14 to the 200k cap (including TP8), and the remaining misses are either a correct final line without `\boxed{}` (3 in DCP2 + MTP, 2 in DCP8) or single-sample arithmetic slips; no run shows degenerate output. The DCP2 + MTP run surfaced one bug, fixed in `28bb3d6074`: the DSA draft's one-shot MHA prefill keyed its prefix all-gather on the global DCP flag instead of the layer's `dcp_size`.

## Checklist

- [x] Format with pre-commit.
- [x] GPU kernel test (localize kernel, folded heads, merged shards vs the unsharded kernel) and a registered 4-GPU GLM-5.3 TP4 + DCP2 + MTP GSM8K test.
- [x] Update `docs/docs/advanced_features/dcp.mdx`.
- [x] Accuracy results (above).

+### DCP × DSA (GLM-5.2, GLM-5.3)
+
+DeepSeek Sparse Attention attends over a top-k slice of the context, so DCP keeps the target's latent KV striped by position while the **index-K cache stays replicated** on every rank: each rank scores the whole sequence, takes the global top-k, and attends over the selected slots it owns. Decode, target verify and extend all follow the same path, so the prefix KV is never gathered.
+
+1. The index-K cache is addressed by the widened virtual slot and costs `c` times its usual share of each rank's KV budget (about 6% at DCP2 and 17% at DCP4 on GLM-5.3).
+2. Each layer maps the global top-k to rank-local rows with one Triton kernel; layers that share the previous layer's top-k reuse the mapping.
+3. The TRT-LLM sparse kernel returns the per-head LSE and the usual DCP merge combines the partial outputs.
+4. The MTP draft (nextn) layer keeps a replicated KV cache over the widened slots and attends without the DCP group, so MTP index share feeds the draft directly.
+
+Requirements: CUDA SM100/SM103 with the `trtllm` DSA backends (selected automatically), an `fp8_e4m3` or `bf16` KV cache, `attn_tp_size % dcp_size == 0`, and, with speculative decoding, the checkpoint's own MTP draft as a single EAGLE chain (`--speculative-eagle-topk 1`, draft tokens equal to steps + 1). HiSparse, prefill CP, HiCache, PD disaggregation, unified memory and `index_kpool > 1` are not supported in this combination.
+
+```bash Command
+sglang serve \
+  --model-path zai-org/GLM-5.3 \
+  --trust-remote-code \
+  --tp-size 8 \
+  --dcp-size 2 \
+  --speculative-algorithm EAGLE \
+  --speculative-num-steps 5 \
+  --speculative-eagle-topk 1 \
+  --speculative-num-draft-tokens 6
+```

+from __future__ import annotations
+
+from typing import Optional
+
+import msgspec
+import torch
+
+from sglang.kernels.ops.attention.dsa.transform_index import (
+    transform_index_page_table_dcp,
+)
+from sglang.kernels.ops.attention.fixup_zero_kv import fixup_zero_kv_rows
+
+TRTLLM_MAX_BATCH_ROWS = 65535
+
+
+class DcpPageTableCache(msgspec.Struct):
+    """NOTE(vincentzed): 57 of GLM's 78 layers reuse the previous layer's top-k
+    tensor; remapping once per fresh top-k cuts 78 launches/step to 21.
+    """
+
+    metadata: object = None
+    layer_id: int = -1
+    topk_indices: Optional[torch.Tensor] = None
+    page_table: Optional[torch.Tensor] = None
+    counts: Optional[torch.Tensor] = None
+
+
+def localize_dcp_page_table(
+    cache: DcpPageTableCache,
+    *,
+    metadata: object,
+    layer_id: int,
+    topk_indices: Optional[torch.Tensor],
+    page_table: torch.Tensor,
+    dcp_size: int,
+    dcp_rank: int,
+) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
+    reuse = (
+        topk_indices is not None
+        and cache.metadata is metadata
+        and cache.layer_id == layer_id - 1
+        and cache.topk_indices is topk_indices
+    )
+    if not reuse:
+        cache.metadata = metadata
+        cache.topk_indices = topk_indices
+        cache.page_table, cache.counts = transform_index_page_table_dcp(
+            page_table, dcp_size, dcp_rank
+        )
+    cache.layer_id = layer_id
+    return cache.page_table, cache.counts
+
+
+def dcp_trtllm_sparse_attention(
+    *,
+    query: torch.Tensor,
+    block_tables: torch.Tensor,
+    seq_lens: torch.Tensor,
+    cu_seqlens_q: torch.Tensor,
+    **attention_kwargs,
+) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
+    import flashinfer.decode
+
+    rows, _, heads, _ = query.shape
+    out_dtype = torch.bfloat16
+    if rows == 0:
+        return (
+            torch.empty(
+                (0, 1, heads, attention_kwargs["kv_lora_rank"]),
+                dtype=out_dtype,
+                device=query.device,
+            ),
+            torch.empty((0, heads), dtype=torch.float32, device=query.device),
+        )
+    lse = torch.empty((rows, heads), dtype=torch.float32, device=query.device)
+    if rows > TRTLLM_MAX_BATCH_ROWS:
+        attention_kwargs["enable_pdl"] = False
+    top_k_lens = attention_kwargs.pop("sparse_mla_top_k_lens", None)
+    outputs = []
+    for start in range(0, rows, TRTLLM_MAX_BATCH_ROWS):
+        end = min(start + TRTLLM_MAX_BATCH_ROWS, rows)
+        output, _ = flashinfer.decode.trtllm_batch_decode_with_kv_cache_mla(
+            query=query[start:end],
+            block_tables=block_tables[start:end],
+            seq_lens=seq_lens[start:end],
+            return_lse=True,
+            lse=lse[start:end],
+            sparse_mla_top_k_lens=(
+                None if top_k_lens is None else top_k_lens[start:end]
+            ),
+            **attention_kwargs,
+        )
+        output = output.view(end - start, heads, -1)
+        fixup_zero_kv_rows(
+            output,
+            lse[start:end],
+            seq_lens[start:end],
+            cu_seqlens_q[: end - start + 1],
+            1,
+        )
+        outputs.append(output)
+    output = outputs[0] if len(outputs) == 1 else torch.cat(outputs)
+    return output.view(rows, 1, heads, -1), lse

What I ran, B300 (SM103), FlashInfer 0.7.0.post1, torch 2.14.1+cu130, `trtllm_batch_decode_with_kv_cache_mla(..., return_lse=True, backend="trtllm-gen")`, compared against a float32 reference:

| Case | Result |
|---|---|
| 32 / 64 / 128 heads, FP8 and BF16, row lengths 1, 3, 16, 63, 64, 65, 200, 2048 | LSE error 0.0000; a 64-head call equals two 32-head calls |
| 64 / 128 heads, batches 1 to 1024, 3 seeds, short / mixed / zero-length rows | no mismatch vs 32-head splits, no NaN |
| your test data: 64 heads, lengths `[1, 63, 64, 0]`, 64-entry KV, 3 repeats, with and without the production counter buffer | correct |

FlashInfer rejects head counts strictly between 64 and 128, so GLM gathers 16, 32 or 64 heads. End to end without folding: TP8 + DCP8 GSM8K 0.943, TP8 + DCP8 + MTP 0.913 (300 questions). The CI kernel test now merges shards at 64 heads.

    rows, _, heads, _ = q.shape
